name: The service serves its own leaf certificate at an anonymous route, and the set-up dialog shows its fingerprint
aliases: server certificate fingerprint in the set-up dialog
summary: A service started with --cert/--key answers GET /v1/service/certificate without a log-in with {"certificate": "<PEM>", "sha256": "<fingerprint>"}: the certificate is the one the TLS handshake presents first, taken from the loaded TLS context by one in-memory ssl.MemoryBIO handshake after load_cert_chain (PEM-encoded by the kit); its fingerprint is the SHA-256 DER hash in openssl's colon form. The --cert file is never read again and no armour is pattern-matched, so a key's DER inside CERTIFICATE armour, a TRUSTED or X509 CERTIFICATE label, an old certificate above the real one and a comment naming the armour lines cannot make the route answer anything but the handshake's first certificate; the private key is never served. There is no size or per-block cap any more (nothing is decoded). Plain http, the tunnel, and a context the handshake cannot be made against answer the ordinary 404, never 500; the service still starts. The dialog shows the fingerprint with a Save button; the prompt writes no settings or certificate file and puts the '# server = ADDRESS' line into the credential file, under umask 077 in a subshell, in PowerShell in its own scope, each line ending with a newline.
